# Algebras & generators

Construct the classical Lie algebras and read off their generators in the standard, Cartan-Weyl, and Chevalley bases.

### LieAlgebra

`LieAlgebra[type, rank]`

The canonical constructor for a simple Lie algebra. `type` is one of the Cartan types and `rank` is a positive integer. Every algebra in the package normalizes to this form, so `SU[n]`, `SO[n]`, and `Sp[n]` are convenience wrappers that evaluate to a `LieAlgebra[...]`.

**Arguments**

| Argument | Description |
| :-- | :-- |
| `type` | the Cartan type: "A", "B", "C", or "D" |
| `rank` | a positive integer, the rank of the algebra |

**Messages**

Emits a message and returns `$Failed` on invalid input.

| Message | When |
| :-- | :-- |
| `LieAlgebra::badtype` | type is not one of "A", "B", "C", "D" |
| `LieAlgebra::badrank` | rank is not a valid rank for the given type |

**Examples**

```{raw} html
<div class="cla-example"><div class="cla-example-row cla-example-in"><div class="cla-example-label">In[1]:=</div><div class="cla-example-cell cla-example-input">
```

```mathematica
SU[3]
```

```{raw} html
</div></div>
```

```{raw} html
<div class="cla-example-row cla-example-out"><div class="cla-example-label">Out[1]=</div><div class="cla-example-cell cla-example-output">
```

```text
LieAlgebra["A", 2]
```

```{raw} html
</div></div></div>
```

```{raw} html
<div class="cla-example"><div class="cla-example-row cla-example-in"><div class="cla-example-label">In[2]:=</div><div class="cla-example-cell cla-example-input">
```

```mathematica
LieAlgebra["B", 2]
```

```{raw} html
</div></div>
```

```{raw} html
<div class="cla-example-row cla-example-out"><div class="cla-example-label">Out[2]=</div><div class="cla-example-cell cla-example-output">
```

```text
LieAlgebra["B", 2]
```

```{raw} html
</div></div></div>
```

**Notes**

- "A" is su, "B" is so of odd dimension, "C" is sp, and "D" is so of even dimension.

**See also:** [`SU`](algebras#su) · [`SO`](algebras#so) · [`Sp`](algebras#sp) · [`Rank`](root-system#rank) · [`CartanMatrix`](root-system#cartanmatrix) · [Concepts: the ABCD classification](../concepts#simple-lie-algebras-and-the-abcd-classification)

### SU

`SU[n]`

The special unitary algebra su(n), the type A(n-1) algebra. Shorthand that normalizes to `LieAlgebra["A", n-1]`.

**Arguments**

| Argument | Description |
| :-- | :-- |
| `n` | an integer >= 2 |

**Messages**

Emits a message and returns `$Failed` on invalid input.

| Message | When |
| :-- | :-- |
| `SU::baddim` | n is not an integer >= 2 |

**Examples**

```{raw} html
<div class="cla-example"><div class="cla-example-row cla-example-in"><div class="cla-example-label">In[1]:=</div><div class="cla-example-cell cla-example-input">
```

```mathematica
SU[3]
```

```{raw} html
</div></div>
```

```{raw} html
<div class="cla-example-row cla-example-out"><div class="cla-example-label">Out[1]=</div><div class="cla-example-cell cla-example-output">
```

```text
LieAlgebra["A", 2]
```

```{raw} html
</div></div></div>
```

```{raw} html
<div class="cla-example"><div class="cla-example-row cla-example-in"><div class="cla-example-label">In[2]:=</div><div class="cla-example-cell cla-example-input">
```

```mathematica

```

### SO

`SO[n]`

The special orthogonal algebra so(n). Covers both families: type B for odd n >= 3 and type D for even n >= 4.

**Arguments**

| Argument | Description |
| :-- | :-- |
| `n` | an integer >= 3 |

**Messages**

Emits a message and returns `$Failed` on invalid input.

| Message | When |
| :-- | :-- |
| `SO::baddim` | n is not an integer >= 3 |

**Examples**

```{raw} html
<div class="cla-example"><div class="cla-example-row cla-example-in"><div class="cla-example-label">In[1]:=</div><div class="cla-example-cell cla-example-input">
```

```mathematica
SO[5]
```

</div></div>
```

```

```text

```

```{raw} html
</div></div></div>
```

```{raw} html
<div class="cla-example"><div class="cla-example-row cla-example-in"><div class="cla-example-label">In[2]:=</div><div class="cla-example-cell cla-example-input">

```

```{raw} html
</div></div></div>
```

**Notes**

- so(odd) and so(even) are different Cartan types (B and D), so their root systems and irreps differ.

**See also:** [`LieAlgebra`](algebras#liealgebra) · [`SU`](algebras#su) · [`Sp`](algebras#sp) · [`Generators`](algebras#generators) · [`Irrep`](representations#irrep)

### Sp

`Sp[n]`

The symplectic algebra sp(n), the type C(n/2) algebra. Defined for even n >= 2.

**Arguments**

| Argument | Description |
| :-- | :-- |
| `n` | an even integer >= 2 (the size of the defining representation) |

**Messages**

Emits a message and returns `$Failed` on invalid input.

| Message | When |
| :-- | :-- |
| `Sp::evenrank` | n is not an even integer >= 2 |

**Examples**

```{raw} html
<div class="cla-example"><div class="cla-example-row cla-example-in"><div class="cla-example-label">In[1]:=</div><div class="cla-example-cell cla-example-input">
```

```mathematica
Sp[4]
```

</div></div></div>

### Generators

`Generators[g]`<br>
`Generators[g, "Standard"]`<br>
`Generators[g, "CartanWeyl"]`<br>
`Generators[g, "Chevalley"]`

The generators of `g` in one of three bases. The scheme defaults to `"Standard"` (`Generators[g]` is `Generators[g, "Standard"]`): the defining-representation generators, as a list of exact matrices. `"CartanWeyl"` and `"Chevalley"` instead return an association with keys `"Cartan"`, `"Raising"`, `"Lowering"`.

**Arguments**

| Argument | Description |
| :-- | :-- |
| `g` | a Lie algebra, e.g. SU[3] |
| `scheme` | optional: "Standard" (default), "CartanWeyl", or "Chevalley" |

**Options**

| Option | Default | Description |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `"Realization"` | `"Diagonal"` | for so/sp in the **Chevalley** scheme, selects the Diagonal realization (diagonal Cartan generators) or the Antisymmetric one; ignored for the Standard/CartanWeyl schemes and for su |

**Messages**

Emits a message and returns `$Failed` on invalid input.

| Message | When |
| :-- | :-- |
| `Generators::badscheme` | the scheme is not "Standard", "CartanWeyl", or "Chevalley" |
| `Generators::badrealization` | "Realization" is not "Diagonal" or "Antisymmetric" (Chevalley scheme of so/sp) |

**Examples**

```{raw} html
<div class="cla-example"><div class="cla-example-row cla-example-in"><div class="cla-example-label">In[1]:=</div><div class="cla-example-cell cla-example-input">
```

```mathematica
Generators[SU[2]]
```

```{raw} html
</div></div>
```

```{raw} html
<div class="cla-example-row cla-example-out"><div class="cla-example-label">Out[1]=</div><div class="cla-example-cell cla-example-output">
```

```text
{{{0, 1/2}, {1/2, 0}}, {{0, -1/2*I}, {I/2, 0}}, {{1/2, 0}, {0, -1/2}}}
```

```{raw} html
</div></div></div>
```

```{raw} html
<div class="cla-example"><div class="cla-example-row cla-example-in"><div class="cla-example-label">In[2]:=</div><div class="cla-example-cell cla-example-input">
```

```mathematica
Keys[Generators[SU[3], "Chevalley"]]
```

```{raw} html
</div></div>
```

```{raw} html
<div class="cla-example-row cla-example-out"><div class="cla-example-label">Out[2]=</div><div class="cla-example-cell cla-example-output">
```

```text
{"Cartan", "Raising", "Lowering"}
```

```{raw} html
</div></div></div>
```

```{raw} html
<div class="cla-example"><div class="cla-example-row cla-example-in"><div class="cla-example-label">In[3]:=</div><div class="cla-example-cell cla-example-input">
```

```mathematica
Generators[SU[3], "Standard"] === Generators[SU[3]]
```

```{raw} html
</div></div>
```

```{raw} html
<div class="cla-example-row cla-example-out"><div class="cla-example-label">Out[3]=</div><div class="cla-example-cell cla-example-output">
```

```text
True
```

```{raw} html
</div></div></div>
```

**Notes**

- The "Realization" option must be given with an explicit scheme, e.g. Generators[g, "Chevalley", "Realization" -> "Antisymmetric"]; passing it with no scheme is read as the scheme argument (a badscheme error). BasisTransform[g] relates the two Chevalley realizations.
- The CartanWeyl and Chevalley shorthands take no options; use Generators[g, ...] directly to pass "Realization".

**See also:** [`CartanWeyl`](algebras#cartanweyl) · [`Chevalley`](algebras#chevalley) · [`BasisTransform`](algebras#basistransform) · [`RepresentationMatrices`](representations#representationmatrices) · [Concepts: the three bases](../concepts#the-three-generator-bases) · [Tutorial: getting started](../tutorials/getting-started)

### CartanWeyl

`CartanWeyl[g]`

Shorthand for `Generators[g, "CartanWeyl"]`. Returns the Cartan-Weyl basis as an association: the diagonal Cartan generators (`"Cartan"`), the raising operators (`"Raising"`), and the lowering operators (`"Lowering"`).

**Arguments**

| Argument | Description |
| :-- | :-- |
| `g` | a Lie algebra |

**Examples**

```{raw} html
<div class="cla-example"><div class="cla-example-row cla-example-in"><div class="cla-example-label">In[1]:=</div><div class="cla-example-cell cla-example-input">
```

```mathematica
Keys[CartanWeyl[SU[2]]]
```

```{raw} html
</div></div>
```

```{raw} html
<div class="cla-example-row cla-example-out"><div class="cla-example-label">Out[1]=</div><div class="cla-example-cell cla-example-output">
```

```text
{"Cartan", "Raising", "Lowering"}
```

```{raw} html
</div></div></div>
```

```{raw} html
<div class="cla-example"><div class="cla-example-row cla-example-in"><div class="cla-example-label">In[2]:=</div><div class="cla-example-cell cla-example-input">
```

```mathematica
CartanWeyl[SU[2]]["Cartan"]
```

```{raw} html
</div></div>
```

```{raw} html
<div class="cla-example-row cla-example-out"><div class="cla-example-label">Out[2]=</div><div class="cla-example-cell cla-example-output">
```

```text
{{{1/Sqrt[2], 0}, {0, -(1/Sqrt[2])}}}
```

```{raw} html
</div></div></div>
```

**Notes**

- A single-argument shorthand: it takes no options. To choose a realization, call Generators[g, "CartanWeyl", ...] directly.

**See also:** [`Generators`](algebras#generators) · [`Chevalley`](algebras#chevalley) · [Guided tour: Cartan-Weyl basis](../walkthrough#cartanweyl-basis)

---

### Chevalley

`Chevalley[g]`

Shorthand for `Generators[g, "Chevalley"]`. Returns the Chevalley basis as an association of `"Cartan"`, `"Raising"`, `"Lowering"` generators, one triple per simple root. This is the basis the representation engine uses; the default (Diagonal) realization has diagonal Cartan generators.

**Arguments**

| Argument | Description |
| :-- | :-- |
| `g` | a Lie algebra |

**Examples**

```{raw} html
<div class="cla-example"><div class="cla-example-row cla-example-in"><div class="cla-example-label">In[1]:=</div><div class="cla-example-cell cla-example-input">
```

```mathematica
Chevalley[SU[2]]
```

```{raw} html
</div></div>
```

```{raw} html
<div class="cla-example-row cla-example-out"><div class="cla-example-label">Out[1]=</div><div class="cla-example-cell cla-example-output">
```

```text
<|"Cartan" -> {{{1, 0}, {0, -1}}}, "Raising" -> {{{0, 1}, {0, 0}}}, 
 "Lowering" -> {{{0, 0}, {1, 0}}}|>
```

```{raw} html
</div></div></div>
```

```{raw} html
<div class="cla-example"><div class="cla-example-row cla-example-in"><div class="cla-example-label">In[2]:=</div><div class="cla-example-cell cla-example-input">
```

```mathematica
DiagonalMatrixQ /@ Chevalley[SO[5]]["Cartan"]
```

```{raw} html
</div></div>
```

```{raw} html
<div class="cla-example-row cla-example-out"><div class="cla-example-label">Out[2]=</div><div class="cla-example-cell cla-example-output">
```

```text
{True, True}
```

```{raw} html
</div></div></div>
```

**Notes**

- A single-argument shorthand: it takes no options. For the Antisymmetric realization of so/sp, call Generators[g, "Chevalley", "Realization" -> "Antisymmetric"]; BasisTransform[g] maps it to the Diagonal one.

**See also:** [`Generators`](algebras#generators) · [`CartanWeyl`](algebras#cartanweyl) · [`RepresentationMatrices`](representations#representationmatrices) · [Guided tour: Chevalley basis](../walkthrough#chevalley-basis)

---

### BasisTransform

`BasisTransform[g]`

The change-of-basis matrix conjugating the Antisymmetric realization of an so/sp Chevalley basis into the Diagonal one (`u.a.Inverse[u]` carries one to the other). For su it is the identity.

**Arguments**

| Argument | Description |
| :-- | :-- |
| `g` | a Lie algebra |

**Examples**

```{raw} html
<div class="cla-example"><div class="cla-example-row cla-example-in"><div class="cla-example-label">In[1]:=</div><div class="cla-example-cell cla-example-input">
```

```mathematica
BasisTransform[SU[2]]
```

```{raw} html
</div></div>
```

```{raw} html
<div class="cla-example-row cla-example-out"><div class="cla-example-label">Out[1]=</div><div class="cla-example-cell cla-example-output">
```

```text
{{1, 0}, {0, 1}}
```

```{raw} html
</div></div></div>
```

```{raw} html
<div class="cla-example"><div class="cla-example-row cla-example-in"><div class="cla-example-label">In[2]:=</div><div class="cla-example-cell cla-example-input">
```

```mathematica
Dimensions[BasisTransform[SO[5]]]
```

```{raw} html
</div></div>
```

```{raw} html
<div class="cla-example-row cla-example-out"><div class="cla-example-label">Out[2]=</div><div class="cla-example-cell cla-example-output">
```

```text
{5, 5}
```

```{raw} html
</div></div></div>
```
